title: Abelian sheaf cohomology vanishes on profinite topological spaces
statement: Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological space (a profinite space). For every abelian sheaf $G$ on the site of open subsets of $X$ with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and every integer $q>0$, $H^q(X,G)=0$, where cohomology is the right derived functor of global sections [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology].

proof.text: For an epimorphism $f:F\to E$ and $e\in E(X)$, use the local-surjectivity characterization in [lem-sc-abelian-sheaf-epi-iff-stalk-epi], implemented by TopCat.Sheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff_epi and TopCat.Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff. For every $x\in X$ choose an open neighbourhood $V_x$ and $s_x\in F(V_x)$ with $f(s_x)=e|_{V_x}$. No module-stalk construction is needed.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-clopen-basis] to choose clopens $x\in C_x\subseteq V_x$ and compactness to extract a finite subcover. Mathlib exists_clopen_partition_of_clopen_cover, specialized with all prescribed closed subsets empty, gives disjoint clopens $D_i\subseteq C_i$ covering $X$. This implements the original elementary finite refinement: subtract preceding clopens successively. Empty pieces and an empty cover are allowed.

Restrict $s_i$ to $D_i$. For unequal indices, $D_i\cap D_j=\varnothing$; the sheaf axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] makes $F(\varnothing)$ terminal, hence zero, so these restrictions agree. For equal indices compatibility is reflexivity. Glue by TopCat.Sheaf.existsUnique_gluing'; naturality of $f$ and uniqueness of gluing show that the glued section maps to $e$. Thus global sections send epimorphisms to surjections, including for empty $X$.

Let $P$ be the sheafification of the free abelian presheaf on the representable of the top open. The sheafification adjunction, free-forgetful adjunction and Yoneda identify $\operatorname{Hom}(P,F)$ with $F(X)$, naturally under postcomposition. This is the representing object in the definition of $H^q(X,F)$ in [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Apply Step 3 to the section corresponding to any map $P\to E$; its lift corresponds to a map $P\to F$ whose composite is the original map. This is exactly the definition of $P$ being projective.

The enough-injectives instance [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives] supplies HasExt in the required universe. By [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], the displayed $H'$ is $\operatorname{Ext}^q(P,G)$, for the projective object of Step 4. The current blueprint clause of [def-pc-ext] says that positive Ext from a projective object is zero; Mathlib Abelian.Ext.subsingleton_of_projective states this directly in the derived-category Ext model. Write $q=n+1$ and apply it. This avoids injective dimension shifting and a separate universal delta functor.
